clue.text: Very dated French king-one must be prosecuted

parts.note: the French phrase très passé means very out of date
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A hopelessly old-fashioned French monarch faces trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a deposed French king; really the clue asks for the French words for very dated, then R. Signs warn that such people will be prosecuted.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices on private land famously warn that intruders will be prosecuted.

clue.text: Muck from isle over river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, so over the second

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Dirt carried from an island across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' places MAN above URE. The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmyard dung is the classic muck spread on fields.

clue.text: Hope to pick girl up going round Sweden

parts.note: to opt is to choose

indicators.note: the turned name goes around the letter for Sweden, enclosing it
in a down clue the girl's name is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Mimi is a girl's name
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to collect a girl on a trip around Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the girl's name round to IMIM, and 'going round' wraps that around the Sweden letter, giving IMISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopefulness and a positive outlook are the same thing.

clue.text: Bend, polling tree

indicators.note: to poll is to cut the top off, so the tree loses its first letter

parts.note: the larch is a conifer

explanation.surface: A bend in the road at a tree used as a polling place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polling' looks electoral, but here it means beheading: LARCH loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved structure, so to arch is to curve.

clue.text: A slinky creature I am, beginning to extend second note in jazz

indicators.note: the run of pieces sits inside the jazz word

parts.note: scat is improvised jazz singing
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word extend is used

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A cat boasts of stretching out a second note in a jazz number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am' reads as the cat speaking, but it is fodder; 'in' puts the run inside the jazz word, splitting it so the breed's second word ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This oriental breed is known for its sleek, lithe body.

clue.text: Grab a few notes

explanation.surface: Seize a fragment of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize suddenly is one sense; a short fragment of song is the other.

clue.text: Reluctant man has to pose with six-footer

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
to sit for a portrait is to pose
an ant, like every insect, has six legs

explanation.surface: An unwilling man has to model alongside a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means a creature with six feet: an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hesitant is unwilling or holding back.

clue.text: Male with short leg

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stage is one leg of a journey

explanation.surface: A man with a stubby leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, or a man alone at a party.

clue.text: Another distribution important, one per variable

indicators.note: something variable can change, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Redistribution matters: each person a different share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' shuffles IMPORTANT + ONE + PER, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing out again means allotting a second time.

clue.text: Small car from the Arabian peninsula

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

explanation.surface: A little vehicle imported from Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Saudi Arabia occupies most of that peninsula, so the adjective describes things from there.

clue.text: Thwart amateur racehorses

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, as in ham actor or radio ham
a trainer's string is their stable of racehorses

explanation.surface: An amateur trainer frustrates a stable of racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring is to cripple or hinder, so to frustrate.

clue.text: A way of gaoling infinitely wealthy statesmen, perhaps

indicators.note: gaoling means locking up, so one word holds another inside

parts.note: a means is a way of doing something

indicators.note: without end, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A method of imprisoning the boundlessly rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infinitely' trims the last letter off the word for wealthy, and 'gaoling' puts the result inside the word for way, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the United States, the States, could jokingly be called statesmen.

clue.text: At regular intervals, maybe the answer release"?

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word maybe, its second and fourth

parts.note: a solution is the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: A setter quips that a regularly spaced answer is a release.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is formal forgiveness, a freeing from guilt or sin.

clue.text: It's vital to try temperature

parts.note: a judge hears a case, that is tries it

explanation.surface: Checking the temperature is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is the courtroom sense: a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is a vital organ, essential to life.

clue.text: Possible readout from 14 monitor is sort of welcome

parts.note: 14 across is an organ also called a ticker
to tape something is to record or monitor it

explanation.surface: A printout from a heart monitor is a kind of greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase 'Possible readout from' is the setter's framing: tape is a readout. A ticker-tape welcome is a parade showered with paper strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroes in New York were greeted by parades showered with strips of stock-price paper.

clue.text: Enjoying painful experiences through chronic stomach acidosis

indicators.note: chronic, in its slang sense of very bad, tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Someone with persistent stomach acid oddly relishes the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pleasure in giving and receiving pain is what the word describes.

clue.text: Help raised for people given torrent of abuse

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a people

explanation.surface: Assistance raised for a tribe that has been insulted.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a tirade.

clue.text: Our silly failing is imagined

indicators.note: failing suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Our foolish shortcomings are only in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory is unreal, a product of the mind.

clue.text: Rubbishing exams and critiques, teaching heads respond

indicators.note: heads means the leading letters of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Head teachers react to criticism of exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teaching heads' reads as head teachers, but 'heads' takes initials of the five words.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something.

clue.text: Game leg fastening device

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A game leg needs a brace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game leg' reads as a lame leg; really it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip that holds a necktie in place is a fastener.

clue.text: 2/3 of piglets allowed nameless one to be the last piggy?

indicators.note: two thirds means only four of the six letters of the word are kept

parts.note: a litter is a brood of piglets
let means allowed

indicators.note: N is short for name, so the word loses that letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme about the last little pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'This little piggy' counts toes, the smallest being the last piggy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the children's rhyme the final toe counted is the smallest one.

clue.text: 1/3 of teenagers (1/2 in theory) develop growing pains

indicators.note: one third of the word, its opening three letters
half the word, its opening three letters

explanation.surface: A third of teenagers, in theory, feel growing pains.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies suffer pain as new teeth come through.

clue.text: US president collects pound for chips

indicators.note: collects means takes inside, so one word holds another

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a US president
a pen or pound is an animal enclosure

explanation.surface: A president gathers money for French fries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is the traditional nickname for a ship's woodworker, not fries; 'pound' is an enclosure, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is old slang for a woodworker, especially aboard ship.

clue.text: Head for garment

explanation.surface: A headdress used as clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland jutting into the sea is one sense; a sleeveless cloak is the other.

clue.text: Foul line

explanation.surface: A dirty row.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means smelly or offensive; it also means a row of soldiers.

clue.text: Something to break, awful waste

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters are in a bad state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A terrible waste that needs breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges WASTE. One breaks a sweat by exerting oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'break a sweat' means start perspiring with effort.

clue.text: Nationalisation — local vessels touring Jersey with it

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one word encloses another

parts.note: liners are ocean ships
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: State takeover of pub ships carrying fashionable Jersey visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests the Channel Island but is the dairy breed; 'touring' puts it inside the ships after their first two letters. A local is British slang for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: When the state takes over an industry it becomes owned by the state.
